field.name: sequenceDefinition
field.purpose: body.sequenceDefinition, projected verbatim like its four siblings, so the review pane can DRAW a call-sequence companion from its source record instead of declaring it unshowable

body.rationale: THREE daemon renderers stamp kind:'diagram-mermaid' — ER (render.ts:104), sequence (:205), component (:243) — but sc1 projects only the ER source record, so a ref's CompanionKind cannot identify which record drew it and the pane cannot draw two of the three. A ledger recount found 5 diagram-mermaid refs against 2 erDefinition bodies and 3 sequenceDefinition bodies, so WITHOUT this field S003 renders 'referenced but could not be shown' on the MAJORITY of documents that carry a diagram — including this Epic's own S002 LLD, whose 'Sequence diagram' companion ref and whose sequenceDefinition sit in the same body, unprojected. ADOPTED IN NARROWED FORM at the S003 approval gate: componentDependencyDefinition was proposed alongside this field and DEFERRED, because the same recount found it in ZERO artifact bodies — projecting it would buy a third derivation, fixtures and visual check for a record no producer has ever emitted. It stays purely additive to add when one first appears. Additive and absent-safe: optional, absence stays an absent key, no existing field changes meaning, no new IPC method, no extra round trip (k2/k7). backwardCompat is symmetric — an older extension ignores the field, and this extension reads it as absent against an un-amended daemon — so no coordinated release is required. sc1 is owned by s1, which is why this is filed as a typed amendment rather than built silently from s3.
